description: The port's recover by its own rule of 2026-11-17 (the user's decision; the original has no recovery), on two commits made here: A, a history of one moment holding k1, and B, a second moment holding k2 and k3, version 2. A sound root header, where reopen would open, is the commit: recover opens at it, cuts what lies past it, and writes nothing, and doesn't go on to a later trailer, even one that verifies, as a trailer's checksum covers the trailer and not the data before it. With ignoring_root_header it goes by the trailers alone, to the last that verifies. Each case is a database of its own, once each way: (a) B past a sound root header at A; (b) the same with B's data zeros, which recovery by the trailers alone goes to, where only what follows from the zeros is read, as reading on would hold a port to taking a pointer of 0 as the file's own header; (c1) past a sound root header, a trailer that verifies with a root tag this version doesn't know, which recover cuts off without looking at, and which with the argument it refuses as opening does, cutting nothing, so that a recover without the argument then cuts it off, the way out for a caller who met the unknown tag; (c2) the root header naming such a trailer, which recover refuses either way, leaving the bytes as they were. recover is only in what the port does, so this is a script only the port runs, whose oracle is run --port.
